e-5450.knowledge_point: Finding the Standard Matrix of a Stretch Transformation Given a Vector and its Image
e-5450.problem: A linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis. Given that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/0adb71786ea5de6203b155882b20000488d5467cf6dfcd34e6fa4e06ec091e46.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/94fb0fd9708c343c89fd98ff5b87c901c9e795026cc1dbd35d29cff92d6fe59e.png) what is the standard matrix of $\mathbf{T}?$
e-5450.worked_solution:
First, we are told that $\mathbf{T}$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis.

Comparing the $x$- and $y$-components of $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}),$ we note the following:

- the $x$-component of $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})$ is $4$ times the $x$-component of $\mathbf{v},$ while

- the $y$-components of $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})$ are the same.

So, we conclude that $\mathbf{T}$ represents a stretch of scale factor $4$ in the $x$-direction. 

Therefore, the standard matrix of $\mathbf{T}$ is

e-5454.knowledge_point: Identifying a Shear or Stretch Transformation Given the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors
e-5454.problem: Consider the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ of $\,\mathbb{R}^2.$ If $\mathbf{T}$ is a linear transformation such that $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{i})=\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{j})=\mathbf{j}$ then, what is the geometric interpretation of the transformation $\mathbf{T}?$
e-5454.worked_solution:
First, let's consider the unit square spanned by the vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/db15a65fd944c24ea2545baea08e6a0789b749295f623d8d4fdc2f07a37d4b73.png)

Now, using the fact that $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{i})=\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{j})=\mathbf{j},$ we can draw the image of the square under the transformation $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/1e5310f50dab35bc25447af9b37d972e11eda0afee98ac99b87a819ba62f56a1.png)

Therefore, the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ represents a vertical shear with a shear factor of $2.$

e-5455.knowledge_point: Identifying a Shear or Stretch Transformation Represented by a Matrix
e-5455.problem:
What linear transformation is represented by the following matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/e335abcb649dae3ed9ade01017a23998614c3d0ff5a0898eb9b4d657f68e8b62.png)
e-5455.worked_solution:
We can find the images of the standard basis vectors $\mathbf i$ and $\mathbf j$ under the action of  $\mathbf T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i \\ T(j) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=2i+j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix represents a *horizontal* shear with a shear factor of $2.$

e-5456.worked_solution:
Looking at the matrix $T,$ we can see that $\mathbf{T}$ represents a vertical shear of shear factor $-1.$ Therefore, the image of the square $R$ under $\mathbf{T}$ is as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/2d3d15c4d6b6f9e08c6fbcc35236b50dcd6cf4d09e9204e0aa255706461c3dd8.png)

$$

First, we are told that T represents a stretch along the x-axis or y-axis.

Comparing the x- and y-components of v and T(v), we note the following:

  • the x-components of v and T(v) are the same, while

  • the y-component of T(v) is 13 times the y-component of v.

content.problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis. Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we are told that $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis.

Comparing the $x$- and $y$-components of $v$ and $T(v),$ we note the following:

- the $x$-components of $v$ and $T(v)$ are the same, while

- the $y$-component of $T(v)$ is $\frac{1}{3}$ times the $y$-component of $v.$

So, we conclude that $T$ represents a stretch of scale factor $\frac{1}{3}$ in the $y$-direction.

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

after.problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis. Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we are told that $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis.

Comparing the $x$- and $y$-components of $v$ and $T(v),$ we note the following:

- the $x$-component of $T(v)$ is $2$ times the $x$-component of $v,$ while

- the $y$-components of $v$ and $T(v)$ are the same.

So, we conclude that $T$ represents a stretch of scale factor $2$ in the $x$-direction. 

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

$[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:

$$

$$

content.problem:
What linear transformation $T$ is represented by the following matrix
$[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
We can find the images of the standard basis vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of  $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=2i \\ T(j) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix represents a stretch of scale factor $2$ in the $x$-direction.
